content: Patients who are younger in age generally achieve more favorable outcomes following surgery, including higher rates of diabetes remission and a reduced likelihood of complications. Individuals with a shorter duration of diabetes prior to surgery also tend to experience better results. Furthermore, patients with less severe forms of diabetes at the time of surgery are more likely to have improved outcomes. Lower levels of baseline visceral fat are another significant factor that contributes to enhanced post-surgical success. Certain populations, such as Asian Americans, demonstrate more substantial benefits from surgery, which may be attributed to distinct metabolic responses unique to these groups.
